tweets.text:
The gacha mechanic is quietly turning into the strongest pmf crypto has seen since perp DEXs and prediction markets.

Look at the pattern: It started with Pokémon cards and some other collectibles. Then comics. Then whiskey, watches, and now the lowest hanging fruit of all: NFTs.

ethereum:0xa0df17b5ac76ababa36e1450e2cbcd18a620c845 is reviving a market everyone had already pronounced dead, purely through gamification. No new narrative, no new drops. Just making it more fun and more liquid.

That’s the whole insight. The gacha loop isn’t a feature, it’s a distribution model. It takes any category with collectors and emotional attachment and turns passive demand into active, addictive engagement.

We call this gamified commerce, and especially as GenZ is slowly but surely taking over, this is going to turn into the new standard for shopping.

I could respect blocking the CLARITY Act over a real ethics concern.

But that’s not what this is. Some of these senators opposed every crypto bill for years, long before Trump ever entered the picture.

And here’s the part they’ll never admit: Trump is fine either way. He made his billy in a year, he’ll make more either way, this bill hardly changes anything for him.

The people who actually lose are the millions of ordinary users who would have finally gotten real regulation and protection that made another FTX impossible. The exact people these senators claim to be fighting for.

Killing the most important consumer protection law in crypto history to score a point against a man it won’t even touch isn’t principle. It’s a grudge with a press release.

Nothing about this protects anyone. It’s just stupid politics and blind hate against crypto.
